text: Titrations using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) can be used to determine the concentration
of metal ions in solution, such as Zn (aq).
A solution of EDTA is usually prepared from the hydrated disodium salt, Na H Y.2H O. The anion of
EDTA is H Y , where Y represents the organic part of the ion.
The equation for the reaction between Zn (aq) and EDTA is shown.
The indicator for the reaction is Solochrome Black, which changes colour at the endpoint from

The term hard water is used to describe water containing the dissolved metal ions, Ca (aq)
2+ 2–
and Mg (aq). Both of these metal ions react with EDTA anions, H Y .
2+ 2+ 2– 2– 2– +
Ca (aq) + Mg (aq) + 2H Y (aq)  CaY (aq) + MgY (aq) + 4H (aq)
In an experiment to determine the concentration of each of these metal ions, two separate
titrations with EDTA need to be performed.
3 –3
For titration 1, a 25.0 cm sample of hard water is titrated with 0.0100 mol dm EDTA solution
using Solochrome Black solution as indicator.
For titration 2, another 25.0 cm sample of the same hard water is first treated with excess
–3 2+
2 mol dm NaOH(aq) which precipitates all of the Mg (aq) ions as Mg(OH) (s). After this
2+ 2+
treatment, no Mg (aq) ions remain in solution, leaving only dissolved Ca (aq) ions in solution.
–3
This solution is then titrated with 0.0100 mol dm EDTA solution using Solochrome Black
solution as indicator.
The following information gives some of the hazards associated with the chemicals used in the
procedure.
–3
Sodium hydroxide Solutions equal to or more concentrated than 0.5 mol dm are
classified as corrosive.
Solochrome Black Solid Solochrome Black is classified as health hazard and is
irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin. All solutions are
made up in ethanol and so are classified as flammable and
health hazard.
